titleEn: The Glory of Kings — The Queen of the South and Tamrin the Merchant (ch. 21–22)
part: ch. 21–22 — The Queen of the South and Tamrin the Merchant
about: The compiler says he found how he was born written in that book, and that the evangelists mention this woman: the Queen of the South will rise on the day of judgment against that generation (Matthew 12:42, Luke 11:31), for she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom; she is the queen of Ethiopia, beautiful, wise and rich, with traders by sea and land. Chapter 22 introduces Tamrin, her chief merchant, with 520 camels and 73 ships, whom Solomon, building the house of God, sends for goods from Arabia; Tamrin goes to Solomon, marvels at his wisdom, justice and gentleness, and the chapter closes on the riches and wisdom God gave Solomon, beyond all kings before or after.

sentences.t: ፳፩ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ንግሥተ ፡ አዜብ ።
sentences.l: 21. Concerning queen-of South.
sentences.i: Chapter 21: Concerning the Queen of the South
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፳፩ is the numeral 20 + 1 = 21. በእንተ 'concerning' governs ንግሥተ 'queen of' (ንግሥት, construct state before the next noun) and አዜብ 'south'; አዜብ 'south' matches the 'queen of the south' of Matthew 12:42 and Luke 11:31 (I have not checked the spelling in the Geʿez Gospels). The text here never says Sheba, and no earlier part of this book names her; the traditional identification of the Gospels' queen with the queen of Sheba of 1 Kings 10 is not made in these two chapters, and the rendering stays with 'South'.

sentences.t: ወዘከመ ፡ ተወልደሂ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ረከብኩ ፡ ጽሑፍ ፡ ውስቴቱ ፡ ለውእቱ ፡ መጽሐፍ ፤
sentences.l: And-how he-was-born-also he, I-found writing within-it, of-that book;
sentences.i: And how he was born, too, I found written within that book;
sentences.n: The speaker is the narrator-compiler (ረከብኩ 'I found', 1cs perfect). ወዘከመ: ወ- 'and' + ዘከመ 'how'. ተወልደ 'he was born' (ተ- passive/reflexive stem of ወለደ), with enclitic -ሂ 'also, too'; ውእቱ 'he' either repeats the subject or is a resumptive 'that' picking up the whole clause ('and how he was born — that I found written …'); the one who was born is not named here (perhaps the Ethiopian king, son of Solomon, of ch. 17–20), so the referent is a reading, not a certainty. ጽሑፍ 'written' (passive participle, 'a writing'); ውስቴቱ 'within it'; ለውእቱ መጽሐፍ 'of that book', ውእቱ here the demonstrative 'that' before a noun.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ከመዝ ፡ ዘከርዋ ፡ ወንጌላዊያን ፡ ለይእቲ ፡ ብእሲት ፤
sentences.l: for thus they-mentioned-her evangelists, of-that woman;
sentences.i: for thus the evangelists mentioned that woman;
sentences.n: ዘከርዋ 'they mentioned her': ዘከረ 'remember, mention' + 3mpl perfect, with the object suffix -ዋ 'her'; ለይእቲ ብእሲት 'that woman' repeats the object with ለ-, as the language often does (the suffix anticipates, the ለ- phrase names). ወንጌላዊያን is the plural of ወንጌላዊ 'evangelist', the Gospel-writers.

sentences.t: ወእግዚእነሂ ፡ ኢየሱስ ፡ ክርስቶስ ፡ ይቤ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይወቅሦሙ ፡ ለሕዝበ ፡ አይሁድ ፡ ሰቃልያን ፡ እለ ፡ አሜሃ ፡ ትውልድ ፡ እንዘ ፡ ይብል ፤
sentences.l: And-our-Lord also Jesus Christ said while he-rebukes-them of-people-of Jews, crucifiers, who then generation, while he-says;
sentences.i: And our Lord Jesus Christ also said, when he was rebuking the people of the Jews, the crucifiers, who were the generation of that time, saying:
sentences.n: ወእግዚእነሂ: ወ- + እግዚእ 'lord' + -ነ 'our' + enclitic -ሂ 'also'. ይወቅሦሙ 'he rebukes them' (ወቀሠ 'blame, rebuke', 3ms imperfect + -ሙ 'them'); እንዘ + imperfect = 'while he …'. ለሕዝበ አይሁድ: ለ- marks the object of the verb; ሕዝበ is the construct 'people of'. ሰቃልያን 'crucifiers' (plural of ሰቃሊ, from ሰቀለ 'hang, crucify'). እለ አሜሃ ትውልድ 'who (were) at that time a generation': no verb, the copula is understood. እንዘ ይብል 'saying' introduces the quotation, which follows in the next unit.

sentences.t: ንግሥተ ፡ አዜብ ፡ ትትነሣእ ፡ አመ ፡ ዕለተ ፡ ኰነኔ ፡ ወትትዋቀሦሙ ፡ ወትትፋትሖሙ ፡ ወትመውኦሙ ፡ ለዛቲ ፡ ትውልድ ፡ እለ ፡ ኢሰምዑ ፡ ስብከተ ፡ ቃልየ ፤
sentences.l: Queen-of South she-will-rise on day-of judgment and-she-will-reproach-them and-she-will-contend-with-them and-she-will-overcome-them, to-this generation who not they-heard preaching-of word-my;
sentences.i: 'The Queen of the South will rise up on the day of judgment, and she will reproach them and contend with them and overcome them — this generation, who did not hear the preaching of my word;
sentences.n: The allusion is Matthew 12:42 and Luke 11:31: 'The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation and shall condemn it.' Here Christ's words are expanded by three verbs, all 3fs imperfect with ወ-: ትትነሣእ 'she will rise' (ተነሥአ 'rise up'), ወትትዋቀሦሙ 'she will reproach them' (the reciprocal ተ- stem of ወቀሠ), ወትትፋትሖሙ 'she will contend with them' (ተፋትሐ, from ፈትሐ 'judge, loose'; 'go to law with'), ወትመውኦሙ 'she will overcome them' (መወአ 'conquer'). Dillmann is unavailable here, so the senses of the last three are unconfirmed; the force 'she will condemn' is what the Gospels say. አመ ዕለተ ኰነኔ 'on the day of judgment' (ዕለተ construct 'day of'). ለዛቲ ትውልድ ('this generation', feminine demonstrative with a feminine noun) stands in apposition to ሙ 'them'. ስብከተ ቃልየ 'the preaching of my word' (ቃል + -የ 'my').

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ለሊሃ ፡ መጽአት ፡ እምአጽናፈ ፡ ምድር ፡ ከመ ፡ ትስማዕ ፡ ጥበቢሁ ፡ ለሰሎሞን ፡ ወዘይቤ ፡ ንግሥተ ፡ አዜብ ፡ ንግሥተ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ይእቲ ፤
sentences.l: for herself she-came from-ends-of earth that she-hear wisdom-his of-Solomon; and-that-which he-said queen-of South queen-of Ethiopia she;
sentences.i: for she herself came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon'; and the one he called 'Queen of the South' is the queen of Ethiopia;
sentences.n: Luke 11:31 (compare Matthew 12:42): she 'came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon.' ለሊሃ 'she herself' (emphatic). መጽአት 'she came' (3fs perfect). እምአጽናፈ ምድር: እም- 'from' + አጽናፈ 'ends of' (construct plural of ጽንፍ). ከመ ትስማዕ 'that she might hear' (jussive). ጥበቢሁ ለሰሎሞን 'his wisdom, Solomon's' — a suffix anticipating the possessor named with ለ-, a pattern that recurs (ch. 17 heading, ch. 1). ወዘይቤ: ወ- + ዘ- 'that which' + ይቤ 'he said', that is, Christ's phrase. ንግሥተ ኢትዮጵያ ይእቲ 'queen of Ethiopia she (is)': the copula ይእቲ follows the predicate.

sentences.t: ወአጽናፈ ፡ ምድርሰ ፡ ዘተብህለ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ድካመ ፡ ፍጥረት ፡ ዘአንስት ፡ ወበእንተ ፡ ርሕቀ ፡ ፍኖት ፡ ወላህበ ፡ ፀሐይ ፡ ወበእንተ ፡ ረኃበ ፡ ፍኖት ፡ ወጽምአ ፡ ማይ ፨
sentences.l: And-ends-of earth-as-for that-which-it-was-said on-account-of weakness-of nature of-women and-on-account-of length-of road and-flame-of sun and-on-account-of hunger-of road and-thirst-of water ፨
sentences.i: And as for 'the ends of the earth', what was said there is on account of the weakness of the female nature, and the length of the road, and the burning of the sun, and on account of the hunger of the road and the thirst for water.
sentences.n: The narrator explains why the Gospel speaks of the 'ends of the earth': the journey was long and hard. ወአጽናፈ ምድርሰ: enclitic -ሰ 'as for'. ዘተብህለ 'that which was said' (ተብህለ, passive of ብህለ 'say'); the sentence has no main verb, 'what was said (is) for …'. Five reasons are linked by ወበእንተ 'and on account of': ድካመ 'weakness of' (construct of ድካም) ፍጥረት ዘአንስት 'nature of women' (ዘ- as a genitive; አንስት is the plural of ብእሲት); ርሕቀ ፍኖት 'distance of the road' (ርሕቀ construct); ላህበ ፀሐይ 'flame of the sun' (ላህብ 'flame, burning heat'); ረኃበ ፍኖት 'hunger of the road'; ጽምአ ማይ 'thirst of water'. ፨ closes the unit.

sentences.t: ወይእቲሰ ፡ ንግሥተ ፡ አዜብ ፡ ሠናይት ፡ ጥቀ ፡ በራእያኒ ፡ በላሕያኒ ፡ ወበአእምሮ ፡ ወልቡና ፡ ዘወሀባ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ከመ ፡ ትሖር ፡ ኢየሩሳሌም ፡ ከመ ፡ ትስማዕ ፡ ጥበቢሁ ፡ ለሰሎሞን ፤
sentences.l: And-she-as-for queen-of South beautiful very in-appearance-both in-comeliness-both and-in-knowledge and-understanding which he-gave-her God that she-go Jerusalem that she-hear wisdom-his of-Solomon;
sentences.i: As for the Queen of the South, she was very beautiful in appearance and in comeliness, and in the knowledge and understanding that God gave her, so that she might go to Jerusalem to hear the wisdom of Solomon;
sentences.n: ወይእቲሰ 'and she, as for her' (ወ- + pronoun + -ሰ, contrastive). ሠናይት ጥቀ 'good, beautiful, very' (fem. adjective; ጥቀ 'very'). በራእያኒ በላሕያኒ: a doubled በ- 'in' with enclitic -ኒ on each, 'both in appearance and in comeliness'; ራእይ 'appearance, sight', ላሕይ 'beauty, comeliness' (the second is read from context and from ላሕዩ 'his beauty' in ch. 22; not confirmed). ዘወሀባ 'which he gave her' (ዘ- + ወሀበ + -ኣ 'her'). ከመ ትሖር 'that she go' (jussive of ሖረ 'go'); Jerusalem is the accusative of place, with no preposition.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ በፈቃደ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ተገብረ ፡ ዝንቱ ፡ ወኮነ ፡ ሥምረቱ ፡ ወይእቲሰ ፡ ባዕልት ፡ ጥቀ ፡ በዘ ፡ ወህባ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ክብረ ፡ ወብዕለ ፡ ወርቀ ፡ ወብሩረ ፡ ወአልባሰ ፡ ክቡረ ፡ ወአግማለ ፡ ወአግብርተ ፡ ወነጋድያነ ፡ ወይነግዱ ፡ ላቲ ፡ ባሕረ ፡ ወየብሰ ፡ ወህንደኬ ፡ ወአስዋነ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: for by-will-of God it-was-done this and-it-was good-pleasure-his, and-she-as-for rich very in-that which he-gave God glory and-wealth, gold and-silver and-garments precious and-camels and-servants and-merchants, and-they-trade for-her sea and-land and-India(?) and-Aswan ፨ ፨
sentences.i: For this was done by the will of God, and it was his good pleasure; and she was very rich in what God had given her — glory and wealth, gold and silver, precious garments, camels, servants and merchants — and they trade for her by sea and by land, and in India(?) and Aswan.
sentences.n: ተገብረ ዝንቱ 'this was done' (ተገብረ, passive of ገብረ 'do, make'); ወኮነ ሥምረቱ 'and it was his pleasure' (ሥምረት 'good pleasure', from ሠምረ). በፈቃደ 'by the will of' (construct). ባዕልት 'rich' (fem.). ወህባ is a spelling of ወሀባ 'he gave her' (as in unit 8). The accusative list ክብረ ወብዕለ ወርቀ ወብሩረ … (the accusative ending, written -ä or -ə after the consonant) stands in apposition to ዘ 'what'. ወይነግዱ ላቲ: 3mpl imperfect of ነገደ 'trade', with ላቲ 'for her' (ለ- with the 3fs suffix); ነጋድያነ 'merchants' is the subject-in-waiting from the list. ባሕረ ወየብሰ 'sea and dry land', accusatives of place: 'by sea and by land'. ህንደኬ I take as a place, India(?): it is not the ህንድ 'India' of ch. 20, and it has the same spelling as the Ethiopic Bible's name for the Candace of Acts 8:27 (from memory of the Geʿez Bible, unchecked), but the trade context and the parallel ወአስዋነ 'Aswan' (Syene, in the south of Egypt, accusative -ነ) favour the place, as given. ፨ ፨ closes the chapter.

sentences.t: ፳፪ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ታምሪን ፡ ነጋዲ ።
sentences.l: 22. Concerning Tamrin merchant.
sentences.i: Chapter 22: Concerning Tamrin the Merchant
sentences.n: Chapter heading. ፳፪ is the numeral 20 + 2 = 22. The heading spells the name ታምሪን, but the body of the chapter has ተምሪን; both are as the source has them, and the English uses Tamrin for both. ነጋዲ 'merchant' (from ነገደ 'trade', the same root as the verb in ch. 21).

sentences.t: ወሀለወ ፡ ፩ ፡ ልብው ፡ ሊቀ ፡ ነጋድያን ፡ ዘስሙ ፡ ተምሪን ፡ ወይጽዕን ፡ ፭፻ ፡ ወ፳ ፡ አግማለ ፡ ወአሕማረኒ ፡ ቦቱ ፡ መጠነ ፡ ፸ወ፫ ፡ ወሰሎሞን ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ አሜሃ ፡ ፈቀደ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይሕንጽ ፡ ቤተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ወለአከ ፡ ውስተ ፡ ኵሉ ፡ ነጋድያን ፡ ለምሥራቅ ፡ ወለምዕራብ ፡ ለደቡብ ፡ ወለሰሜን ፡ ከመ ፡ ይምጽኡ ፡ ነጋድያን ፡ ወይንሥኡ ፡ በኀቤሁ ፡ ወርቀ ፡ ወብሩረ ፡ ወውእቱኒ ፡ ይንሣእ ፡ ዘይትፈቀድ ፡ ለግብር ፡ ወነገርዎ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ነጋዲ ፡ ኢትዮጵያዊ ፡ ባዕል ፡ ወለአከ ፡ ከመ ፡ ያምጽእ ፡ ሎቱ ፡ ዘይትፈቀድ ፡ እምብሔረ ፡ ዐረብ ፡ ወርቀ ፡ ቀዪሐ ፡ ወዕፀ ፡ ዘኢይነቅዝ ፡ ጸሊመ ፡ ወሰንፔረ ፡ ።
sentences.l: And-there-was one prudent chief-of merchants whose-name Tamrin, and-he-loads 520 camels and-ships-also with-him as-many-as 73; and-Solomon king then he-wished that he-build house-of God, and-he-sent among all merchants to-east and-to-west, to-south and-to-north, that they-come merchants and-they-take with-him gold and-silver, and-he-also he-takes what is-needed for-work; and-they-told-him concerning that merchant Ethiopian rich, and-he-sent that he-bring to-him what is-needed from-land-of Arabia: gold red and-wood which-not-it-rots black and-sapphire. ።
sentences.i: There was a prudent man, chief of merchants, whose name was Tamrin, who loaded 520 camels, and he had ships as well, as many as 73. And Solomon the king, at that time, wished to build the house of God, and sent word to all the merchants, east and west, south and north, that the merchants should come and take from him gold and silver, and that he, for his part, would take what was needed for the work; and they told him about that Ethiopian merchant, a rich man, and he sent that he should bring him what was needed from the land of Arabia — red gold, and black wood that does not rot, and sapphire.
sentences.n: The unit runs to about 62 words with no ፤ in it, and it ends at the ። the source gives here, so it is longer than the ~45-word rule allows. ወሀለወ 'and there was/existed'; ፩ is the numeral 1 ('one', here 'a certain'); ልብው 'prudent, wise'; ሊቀ ነጋድያን 'chief of merchants' (ሊቀ construct); ዘስሙ 'whose name'. ወይጽዕን 'and he loads' (ጸዐነ 'carry, load', 3ms imperfect, said of one who loads 520 camels, an owner of caravans); ፭፻ ወ፳ is 500 and 20 = 520, ፸ወ፫ is 70 and 3 = 73 (ወ between numerals is 'and'). ወአሕማረኒ ቦቱ 'and ships too (አሕማር, plural of ሐመር) were with him, he had', with መጠነ 'to the measure of, as many as'. Solomon's building of the Temple (1 Kings 5–6; 2 Chronicles 2) is the setting. ወለአከ 'and he sent' (ለአከ, the same verb as ወለአከ later in the unit). ውስተ ኵሉ ነጋድያን ለምሥራቅ … 'among all the merchants, to the east, to the west, to the south and to the north' (the four directions with ለ-). ወይንሥኡ በኀቤሁ ወርቀ ወብሩረ: I read በኀቤሁ as 'from him' and ይንሥኡ 'they take' (jussive), which is uncertain; another reading is 'take (it) to him' (as ኀቤሁ means 'to him' elsewhere). ዘይትፈቀድ 'what is needed' (passive imperfect of ፈቀደ, 'what is wished/required'); ለግብር 'for the work'. ወነገርዎ 'and they told him'. ከመ ያምጽእ ሎቱ 'that he bring him' (አምጽአ, the causative of መጽአ). ብሔረ ዐረብ 'land of the Arabs/Arabia'. ቀዪሐ 'red' (accusative of ቀይሕ); ዘኢይነቅዝ ጸሊመ 'which does not rot, black' — the black wood that does not rot is perhaps ebony (my inference). ሰንፔረ 'sapphire' (a loanword). The stray ፡ before ። is as the source has it.

sentences.t: ወሖረ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ነጋዲ ፡ ዘስሙ ፡ ተምሪን ፡ ነጋዲሃ ፡ ለንግሥተ ፡ ኢትዮጵያ ፡ ኀበ ፡ ሰሎሞን ፡ ንጉሥ ፤
sentences.l: And-he-went that merchant whose-name Tamrin, merchant-her of-queen-of Ethiopia, to Solomon king;
sentences.i: And that merchant, whose name was Tamrin, the queen of Ethiopia's merchant, went to King Solomon;
sentences.n: ነጋዲሃ ለንግሥተ ኢትዮጵያ 'her merchant, the queen of Ethiopia's': the suffix -ሃ 'her' anticipates the possessor named with ለ-, as in ch. 21 (ጥበቢሁ ለሰሎሞን). ኀበ 'to, toward'. ሖረ 'he went'.

sentences.t: ወነሥአ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ዘፈቀደ ፡ እምኔሁ ፡ ወወሀቦ ፡ ለነጋዲ ፡ ዘይፈቅድ ፡ አፈድፍዶ ፡ እምንዋዩ ፡ ወውእቱሰ ፡ ነጋዲ ፡ ልብው ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ ወይሬኢ ፡ ጥበቢሁ ፡ ለሰሎሞን ፡ ወያነክር ፡ ወይትዐቀብ ፡ ከመ ፡ ይጠይቅ ፡ አውሥኦተ ፡ ቃሉ ፡ ወፍትሖ ፡ ወሣእሣአ ፡ አፉሁ ፡ ወጣዕመ ፡ ነገሩ ፡ ወሑረቶ ፡ ወንብረቶ ፡ ወተንሥኦቶ ፡ ወግብሮ ፡ ወፍቅሮ ፡ ወሥርዐቶ ፡ ወማእዶ ፡ ወሕጎ ፡ ወለእለኒ ፡ ይኤዝዞሙ ፡ ምስለ ፡ ትሕትና ፡ ወየውሀት ፤
sentences.l: And-he-took all what he-wished from-him, and-he-gave-to-the-merchant what he-wishes, abundantly, from-his-goods; and-he-as-for merchant prudent exceedingly, and-he-sees wisdom-his of-Solomon and-he-marvels and-he-takes-care that he-observe answering-of word-his and-judgment-his and-the-[śāʾśāʾa]-of mouth-his and-sweetness-of speech-his and-going-his and-sitting-his and-rising-his and-deed-his and-love-his and-ordinance-his and-table-his and-law-his, and-also-those he-commands-them with humility and-meekness;
sentences.i: And Solomon took from him all that he wished, and gave the merchant what he wished, abundantly, out of his own goods; and the merchant, for his part, was exceedingly prudent, and he saw the wisdom of Solomon and marvelled, and took care to examine the reply of his word, and his judgment, and the [śāʾśāʾa] of his mouth(?), and the sweetness of his speech, and his goings, and his sitting, and his rising, and his deeds, and his love, and his ordinances, and his table, and his law; and also how he commands those under him, with humility and gentleness;
sentences.n: The subject of ወነሥአ and ወወሀቦ is not marked: I read Solomon as the one who took what he wished from Tamrin and gave him, in return, what he wished, out of his goods (ንዋዩ 'his goods', ንዋይ + -ሁ); the other reading, Tamrin as the taker, is possible. አፈድፍዶ 'abundantly' (a gerund of the causative of ፈደፈደ 'increase'). ወውእቱሰ ነጋዲ 'and the merchant, for his part' (ውእቱ + -ሰ). ወይሬኢ 'and he saw' (ርእየ), here the imperfect used as a narrative past, as are ወያነክር 'and he marvelled' (አነከረ 'wonder, marvel') and ወይትዐቀብ 'and he took care'. ከመ ይጠይቅ 'that he examine' (ጠየቀ 'examine, investigate'). What follows is a list of accusatives, each with the suffix -ሁ/-ኦ 'his': አውሥኦተ ቃሉ 'the answering of his word', ፍትሖ 'his judgment', ጣዕመ ነገሩ 'the sweetness of his speech', ሑረቶ 'his goings, his conduct' (ሑረት, from ሖረ), ንብረቶ 'his sitting, his manner of living' (ንብረት), ተንሥኦቶ 'his rising', ግብሮ 'his deed', ፍቅሮ 'his love', ሥርዐቶ 'his ordinance', ማእዶ 'his table' (ማእድ), ሕጎ 'his law'. ሣእሣአ አፉሁ: I cannot confirm ሣእሣእ (Dillmann is unavailable here); I leave it bracketed and guess 'the [śāʾśāʾa] of his mouth' to mean something like the fitness or order of his speech, which is uncertain. The ለእለኒ 'and also those whom' (ለ- object marker + እለ + -ኒ) ይኤዝዞሙ 'he commands them' (አዘዘ 'command'); ትሕትና 'humility', የውሀት 'meekness, gentleness' (from የዋህ).

sentences.t: ወሶበኒ ፡ አበሱ ፡ ይምሕሮሙ ፡ እስመ ፡ በጥበብ ፡ ወበፍርሀተ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ይሠርዕ ፡ ቤቶ ፤
sentences.l: And-even-when they-sinned he-pities-them for with-wisdom and-with-fear-of God he-orders house-his;
sentences.i: And even when they sinned he has pity on them, for with wisdom and with the fear of God he orders his house;
sentences.n: ወሶበኒ 'and even when' (ሶበ 'when' + enclitic -ኒ). አበሱ 'they sinned' (አበሰ 'sin', 3mpl perfect; I take the initial አ as part of the root, not a causative prefix). ይምሕሮሙ 'he pities them' (ምሕረ 'have mercy, forgive', 3ms imperfect + -ሙ; spelled with ሕ, which marks this root and not ምህረ 'teach'). በፍርሀተ እግዚኣብሔር 'in the fear of God' (ፍርሀተ construct). ይሠርዕ ቤቶ 'he orders his house' (ሠርዐ 'set in order, appoint'; ቤቶ is the accusative of ቤቱ 'his house' (ቤት + -ሁ), the object of ይሠርዕ, as with the accusatives of unit 13). Proverbs 1:7, 'the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom', may lie behind the pairing.

sentences.t: ወያክሞስሶሙ ፡ በየውሀት ፡ ለአብዳን ፡ ወይሤርሖን ፡ በየውሀት ፡ ለአእማት ፡ ወይከሥት ፡ አፉሁ ፡ በአምሳል ፤
sentences.l: and-he-[yakmossomu]-them with-meekness to-fools and-he-arranges-them with-meekness to-maidservants, and-he-opens mouth-his in-parable;
sentences.i: he deals(?) with the fools with gentleness, and sets(?) the maidservants in order with gentleness, and opens his mouth in a parable;
sentences.n: ያክሞስሶሙ I cannot place (the shape is ያ- 'he' + a stem + -ሙ 'them'; whether the stem is a quadriliteral I cannot tell, and Dillmann is unavailable here); 'deals with' is only a placeholder for a verb of manner, since በየውሀት 'with gentleness' supplies the manner. አብዳን 'fools' (plural of አብድ); አእማት 'maidservants' (plural of አመት). The ለ- on each repeats the object named by the suffix, as in unit 3. ይሤርሖን 'he arranges them (f.)' (ሠርሐ 'make ready, set in order', with the 3fp suffix -ሖን), also uncertain in sense. ወይከሥት አፉሁ በአምሳል 'and he opens his mouth in a parable': አምሳል is 'likeness, parable', and the phrase recalls Psalm 78:2 (77:2 in the Septuagint), 'I will open my mouth in a parable', quoted of Christ in Matthew 13:35; I think it is an echo, not a quotation.

sentences.t: ወይጥዕም ፡ ቃሉ ፡ እምጸቃውዐ ፡ መዓር ፡ ወኵሉ ፡ ግብሩ ፡ ፍትው ፡ ወኵሉ ፡ ርእየቱ ፡ አዳም ፤
sentences.l: and-it-is-sweet word-his than-honeycomb(?) of-honey, and-all deed-his desirable, and-all appearance-his pleasing(?);
sentences.i: his word is sweeter than the honeycomb(?) of honey, and all his deeds are desirable, and all his appearance is comely(?);
sentences.n: ይጥዕም 'it is sweet' (ጠዐመ); እም- before the noun means 'than'. ጸቃውዐ መዓር 'the [ṣäqawʿa] of honey': I take ጸቃውዕ as 'honeycomb' from the sense and from Psalm 19:10 (18:11 in the Septuagint), 'sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb', but cannot confirm the word. ፍትው 'desirable, fitting'. ርእየቱ 'his appearance' (ርእየት). አዳም is uncertain: it can be the name Adam, but standing alone as the predicate it more likely means 'pleasing, comely' (as I give it); another reading, 'all his appearance is (that of) Adam' as the first, perfect man, is not impossible.

sentences.t: እስመ ፡ ትትፈቀር ፡ ጥበብ ፡ በኀበ ፡ ማእምራን ፡ ወትትሜነን ፡ በኀበ ፡ አብዳን ፡ ወዘንተ ፡ ኵሎ ፡ ርኢዮ ፡ ያስተዐጽብ ፡ ውእቱ ፡ ነጋዲ ፡ ወያነክር ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ እስመ ፡ ለእለ ፡ ይሬእይዎ ፡ ኵለንታሁ ፡ መፍትው ፡ ወመምህር ፡ ውእቱ ፤
sentences.l: for she-is-loved wisdom among knowers and-she-is-rejected among fools; and-this all having-seen he-is-astonished that merchant and-he-marvels exceedingly, for to-those who-see-him all-of-him desirable and-teacher he;
sentences.i: for wisdom is loved among the knowing and scorned among fools; and seeing all this, the merchant was astonished and marvelled exceedingly, for to those who see him he is altogether desirable, and a teacher;
sentences.n: ትትፈቀር 'she is loved' (ተፈቀረ) — ጥበብ 'wisdom' is feminine and takes feminine verbs. ትትሜነን 'she is rejected, scorned' (ተመነነ; sense from context, not confirmed). በኀበ 'among, in the presence of'. ማእምራን 'those who know' (plural of ማእምር). ርኢዮ 'having seen' (the 3ms gerund of ርእየ; its ending -ዮ is the gerund's own, not an object suffix, and the object is ወዘንተ ኵሎ 'and this all'). ያስተዐጽብ 'he was astonished' (አስተዐጸበ; I take it as 'marvel'). ኵለንታሁ 'all of him, his whole self'. መፍትው 'desirable, worthy' and መምህር 'teacher' (ምህረ 'teach').

sentences.t: ወእለኒ ፡ በጽሑ ፡ ኀቤሁ ፡ ኢይፈቅዱ ፡ ይእትቱ ፡ ወይትገሐሡ ፡ እምኔሁ ፡ በእንተ ፡ ጥበቡ ፡ ወላሕዩ ፤
sentences.l: and-those-also who-arrived to-him not they-wish they-leave and-they-withdraw from-him on-account-of wisdom-his and-comeliness-his;
sentences.i: and those too who have come to him do not wish to leave(?) him and withdraw from him, because of his wisdom and his comeliness;
sentences.n: ወእለኒ 'and those too' (እለ + -ኒ). በጽሑ 'they arrived' (በጽሐ). ኢይፈቅዱ 'they do not wish', with the jussive ይእትቱ 'that they leave' (the sense 'leave' comes only from the pairing with the next verb; the form ends in -ቱ, so its last root consonant is ተ, which does not fit እተወ — that would give ይእትዉ — and I cannot place the root; Dillmann is unavailable here) and ይትገሐሡ 'that they draw back' (ተገሕሠ 'withdraw, go away'). ላሕዩ 'his comeliness, beauty', as in ch. 21.

sentences.t: ወጣዕመ ፡ ነገሩ ፡ ከመ ፡ ማይ ፡ ለጽሙእ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ኅብስት ፡ ለ ፡ ርኁብ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ፈውስ ፡ ለድዉይ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ልብስ ፡ ለዕሩቅ ፡ ወከመ ፡ አብ ፡ ለእጓለ ፡ ማውታ ፤
sentences.l: and-sweetness-of speech-his like water for-the-thirsty and-like bread for-the-hungry and-like healing for-the-sick and-like clothing for-the-naked and-like father for-child-of the-dead;
sentences.i: and the sweetness of his speech is like water to the thirsty, and like bread to the hungry, and like healing to the sick, and like clothing to the naked, and like a father to the orphan;
sentences.n: A run of ከመ 'like' phrases, each with ለ- 'to, for': ጽሙእ 'thirsty', ርኁብ 'hungry', ድዉይ 'sick', ዕሩቅ 'naked'. In the source ለ ርኁብ has a stray wordspace. እጓለ ማውታ 'child of the dead', the idiom for 'orphan' (ማውታ is the plural of ሙት; the construct form of እጓል is እጓለ). The sequence may recall the works of mercy of Matthew 25:35–36 (food, drink, clothing, the sick) and, in part, Isaiah 58:7 (bread for the hungry, covering the naked); the text does not quote either.

sentences.t: ወይፈትሕ ፡ በጽድቅ ፡ ወኢያደሉ ፡ ለገጽ ፤
sentences.l: and-he-judges in-righteousness and-not-he-inclines to-face;
sentences.i: and he judges in righteousness, and does not show partiality;
sentences.n: ወይፈትሕ 'and he judges' (ፈትሐ). ኢያደሉ 'he does not incline' (አደለወ 'incline, weigh'; ኢ- negative); ለገጽ 'to the face' is the idiom for partiality, 'respect of persons' (Deuteronomy 1:17, Proverbs 24:23).

sentences.t: ወቦቱ ፡ ክብረ ፡ ወብዕለ ፡ ዘወሀቦ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ፈድፋደ ፡ ወርቀ ፡ ወብሩረ ፡ ወዕንቈ ፡ ወአልባሰ ፡ ክቡረ ፡ ወእንስሳ ፡ ወአራዊት ፡ ዘአልቦ ፡ ኆልቈ ፡ ወበመዋዕሊሁሰ ፡ ለሰሎሞን ፡ ንጉሥ ፡ ኮነ ፡ ወርቅ ፡ ከመ ፡ ብርት ፡ ወብሩር ፡ ከመ ፡ ዐረር ፡ ወብርትሰ ፡ ወዐረር ፡ ወኀጺን ፡ ኮነ ፡ ብዝኁ ፡ ከመ ፡ ዕፀ ፡ ባሕሩስ ፡ ወከመ ፡ ብርዐ ፡ ገዳም ፡ ወዕፀ ፡ ቄድሮስኒ ፡ ብዙኀ ፡ ኮነ ፤
sentences.l: And-with-him glory and-wealth which he-gave-him God exceedingly, gold and-silver and-stones and-garments precious and-livestock and-wild-beasts which there-is-not number; and-in-days-his-as-for of-Solomon king it-became gold like [bərt] and-silver like bronze(?) and-[bərt]-as-for and-bronze(?) and-iron it-became plentiful like trees-of [bahrus] and-like [bərʿa]-of wilderness and-trees-of cedar-also plentiful it-became;
sentences.i: And he had glory and wealth, which God had given him in abundance — gold and silver and gems and precious garments, and livestock and wild beasts without number. And in the days of Solomon the king gold became like [bərt] and silver like bronze(?), and as for [bərt] and bronze(?) and iron, they became as plentiful as the [bahrus] trees and as the [bərʿa] of the wilderness, and cedar wood too became abundant;
sentences.n: The unit is about 40 words. ወቦቱ 'and with him (were)', that is, 'he had' (the preposition በ- with the 3ms suffix). ዘወሀቦ 'which he gave him'. ዕንቈ 'gems' (accusative of ዕንቊ 'gem', used collectively); ወእንስሳ 'and livestock'; ወአራዊት 'and wild beasts'; ዘአልቦ ኆልቈ 'which has no number'. ወበመዋዕሊሁሰ ለሰሎሞን ንጉሥ 'and in his days, Solomon the king's' (suffix anticipating the possessor). Compare 1 Kings 10:27 and 2 Chronicles 1:15 (silver as common as stones, cedar as sycamores). The metal and plant words are uncertain: ብርት is a rare word that I cannot confirm (a metal; I leave it bracketed); ዐረር is 'bronze' or 'brass'; ኀጺን 'iron'. ባሕሩስ (trees) and ብርዐ (of the wilderness) I cannot place; the second may be 'sand' or 'dust', which would fit the comparison, and ባሕሩስ may be a tree name, and both are bracketed. ዕፀ ቄድሮስ 'cedar wood' (ቄድሮስ from the Greek kedros); ብዙኀ ኮነ 'became abundant'.

sentences.t: በዘ ፡ ወሀቦ ፡ እግዚኣብሔር ፡ ክብረ ፡ ወብዕለ ፡ ወጥበበ ፡ ወሞገሰ ፡ ዘኢኮኑ ፡ ከማሁ ፡ እለ ፡ እምቅድሜሁ ፡ ወኢይከውኑ ፡ እምድኅሬሁ ፡ ዘከማሁ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.l: by-that-which he-gave-him God glory and-wealth and-wisdom and-majesty such-as not-they-were like-him those who before-him and-not they-will-be after-him such-as-he ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨ ፨
sentences.i: by what God gave him — glory, wealth, wisdom and majesty — such that those before him were not like him, and none such as he will be after him.
sentences.n: በዘ ወሀቦ 'by that which he gave him' (በ- + ዘ- + ወሀበ + -ኦ). ሞገሰ 'majesty, favour' (accusative of ሞገስ). ዘኢኮኑ ከማሁ እለ እምቅድሜሁ 'such that those before him were not like him' (ከማሁ 'like him'; ኮኑ 3mpl perfect of ኮነ). ኢይከውኑ እምድኅሬሁ ዘከማሁ 'there will not be after him one like him' (3mpl imperfect of ኮነ). The ten ፨ at the end of the chapter close the part. The same line, about Solomon's incomparable wisdom, echoes 1 Kings 3:12 and 10:23.
